newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close up sharply, set new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close up sharply, set new highs.

text.p: CME pork belly futures ran up for limit gains late and set new highs before closing sharply higher. Hog futures recovered late to end mixed aftr early profit taking and setting of new highs, traders said.

Pork belly futures closed up 2.700 to one cent, with May up 2.400 at 89.950 cents a lb after rising the daily limit to a new high of 90.550 cents. All months posted new highs with July, August and March also limit up briefly.
Hog futures ended up 0.300 to off 0.350 cent, with June off 0.125 at 85.325 cents after setting a new contract high early of 85.700. July also posted a new high of 85.450 cents.

Profit taking hit pork bellies for a time early, but prices rallied for limit gains and new contract highs late before profit taking pared best levels at the close. Futures filled the gap left in the charts from the opening bulge to new highs and then ran up again based on further gains in cash bellies, Japan product buying and generally bullish expectations for the monthly Cold Storage report, they said.

"You have new elements of demand in the market and people are trying to assess how much that means for bellies, which could be anywhere from five to 20 cents," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Analyst expectations on the amount of bellies in U.S. warehouses as of April 1 in the USDA report ranged from 49 to 53.2 million lbs versus 47.655 million on hand last year.

The report would have to show storings above the high end of expectations to be remotely considered bearish as there have been very little product put into storage during April. Stocks could easily fall back below year ago levels during April which would be very bullish of prices going into the peak summer demand season, traders added.

Prudential Securities notably bought at the start before selling by Rand Financials and R.J. O'Brien took prices down below previous levels. General demand then boosted the market going into midsession and new buy stops lifted prices to new highs again late, pit sources said.

Hog futures retreated after briefly posting gains near the opening as profit taking and speculative selling developed. But the rally in pork bellies spilled over and futures closed mostly higher despite short hog futures/long pork belly futures spreading, traders said.
Hog futures were reaching a near term top. The potential for further gains was limited especially with futures already trading live hog prices in the mid $60's per cwt, they said.

However, cash hog prices will likely continue to trend up to the mid $60 and underlying support in deferred contracts should remain from expectations that international demand for U.S. pork products will be strong this year following the Taiwan and Netherlands pork bans, they added.

Rand Financials and Lind-Waldock sold June while RBH sold July and Cargill Investor Services was on both sides of the market early. ABN Chicogo Corp and Smith Barney bought August and October. In hog options, commission houses were offering 86 and higher June calls and buying 82 puts, pit sources said.
